name: Rich text editor
purpose: Write a formatted project description and read the saved result.
notes: A compact toolbar supports bold, italic, lists, links and undo/redo. Keyboard shortcuts and pasted content use the same Tiptap schema.
The JSON document is the source of truth. Cards derive plain-text previews; details render the supported formatting.
Save keeps this example’s content; Cancel discards edits. Project forms also retain drafts during navigation.

name: Button
purpose: Give the primary action clear emphasis and keep secondary actions quieter.
notes: Use a button for an action and a link for navigation.
Label icon-only actions. Disabled controls cannot receive normal keyboard focus.
While a result is pending, loading keeps the label's width and shows a spinner, so neighbouring controls stay put.

name: Input
purpose: Collect a short value with a visible label and an associated validation message.
notes: Size the field for its expected content, not the entire available surface.
This example uses native email validation on submit and focuses the invalid field. It saves only inside this preview.

name: Select
purpose: Choose one value from a list of known options.
notes: Arrow keys move through options; Enter selects and Escape dismisses.
Pass the items to Base UI so the trigger shows the label rather than an internal ID.

name: Checkbox
purpose: Choose independent options or select records for a shared action.
notes: Each checkbox has its own visible label; Space changes its checked state.
Related choices belong in a fieldset with a legend. Table selection may also use an indeterminate state.

name: Radio Group
purpose: Choose exactly one option from a small visible set.
notes: Use a group label and keep every option's label clickable.
Arrow keys move the selection; Tab leaves the group.

name: Dialog
purpose: Complete a focused task while preserving the surrounding page.
notes: Provide a title, a visible close control and a clear completion action.
Cancel and Escape discard this preview's rename draft. Saving updates its title; closing returns focus to Rename.

name: Tabs
purpose: Switch between related panels within one page.
notes: Use route links for destinations, and tabs for related content panels.
This example uses manual activation: arrow keys move focus, then Enter or Space activates a panel.

name: Alert
purpose: Explain a consequential problem and offer an action that resolves it.
notes: Use assertive announcements for errors that need attention; routine completion can use a polite status.
Retry here resolves a local example. It does not contact a service.

name: Empty
purpose: Distinguish no results from an empty account and provide the right next action.
notes: A no-results state should let the person change or clear the filter.
This preview starts with a nonmatching query against the same project fixture used by the demo.

name: Table
purpose: Compare structured records with aligned headers and values.
notes: The primitive supplies table semantics. Sorting, filters and pagination belong to the composed data view.
Numeric values align to the end. Narrow tables scroll inside their own container.

name: Tooltip & text hint
purpose: Reveal a brief explanation on demand without shifting the surrounding layout.
notes: Dotted-underlined text opens a hoverable popover; activate it by tap, Enter or Space. Escape and outside interaction dismiss it.
Icon tooltips supplement accessible labels. Required instructions and errors stay visible.

name: Switch
purpose: Turn a setting on or off where the change applies to a saved preference.
notes: Use a switch for an on/off setting and a checkbox for picking items or agreeing to terms.
Pair each switch with a visible label; the whole row can carry a short description.

name: Progress
purpose: Show how far a measurable piece of work has come.
notes: Name what is measured and show the value as text; the bar alone is decoration.
Set --progress-color to tie a bar to its record, such as a project's colour.

name: Keyboard key
purpose: Show the keys for a shortcut next to the action it performs.
notes: Group the keys of one shortcut; show the platform's modifier where it differs.
A hint supplements the action's name and aria-keyshortcuts; it never replaces them.

name: Toast
purpose: Confirm a completed action briefly and offer to undo it.
notes: Use a toast when the result is not visible where the person acted, or to offer Undo. Keep errors that block progress inline.
Toasts stack in the corner, pause while hovered or focused, and F6 moves focus into them.

name: Date picker
purpose: Pick a single calendar date from a field-sized trigger.
notes: The value is an ISO date string; a hidden input carries it inside a form.
Pass labelledBy so the field name and the chosen date are both announced. Arrow keys move between days; Enter picks.

name: Date range picker
purpose: Pick a first and last day for a report in two clicks.
notes: Each opening starts a fresh range; the second day applies it and Escape keeps the current one.
latest and maxDays keep the range inside the data that exists.

name: Carousel
purpose: Browse a row of related cards one page at a time.
notes: Built on native scroll snapping: swipe, trackpad and keyboard scrolling work, and Previous/Next move one visible page, disabled at the ends.
The carousel and each slide are named (slide 2 of 4); keep cards readable without the controls, and never auto-advance.

name: Hover card
purpose: Preview who or what a link leads to before following it.
notes: The trigger is a real link; the card opens on hover or keyboard focus after a short delay and closes when the pointer or focus leaves.
Touch devices and screen readers follow the link without seeing the card, so the card may only repeat or summarise, never hold the sole copy of information or an action.

name: Context menu
purpose: Offer an item's actions where the pointer is, on right-click, long press or the context-menu key.
notes: Shares the dropdown menu's items and styling, so one action list can serve a visible menu button and the context menu.
It is a shortcut: every action also needs a visible control, because long press and the context-menu key are not discoverable.

name: Scroll area
purpose: Scroll a bounded list with a thin overlay scrollbar that takes no layout space.
notes: Scrolling stays native (wheel, touch, keyboard); the viewport becomes focusable only when it overflows. Name it as a region when its content is a distinct list.
Base UI keeps the root relatively positioned, so place it with a wrapper. The viewport exposes --scroll-area-overflow-y-start/-end for edge fades.

name: Drawer
purpose: Bring a short set of choices up from the screen edge on phones.
notes: A modal panel with a title, a swipe handle and a clear close action; Escape, the overlay and a swipe down also close it, returning focus to the trigger.
Choices apply as they change; the close button can say what the result will be, such as Show 4 projects. Use a Sheet for longer side panels.

name: Code block
purpose: Show code with syntax highlighting, a file or language label and a copy button.
notes: Highlighting loads on first use and takes its colours from the --syntax-* tokens, so code follows light, dark and the accent. The block renders plain text first, at the same size.
Long lines scroll inside the block, which takes keyboard focus. Copy reports success in place; when the clipboard refuses, the code is selected instead.

name: Snippet
purpose: Give one command or line of code with a copy button.
notes: The prefix, such as $, is shown but not copied.
Name what is copied with label; the button then reads Copy install command.

name: Prompt input
purpose: Write a message to a model, with attachments and tools, and stop its reply.
notes: A rounded surface: attachments, the text, then a row with the + menu (files, and any records you offer as context), your tools and the round send button. Files can also be dropped or pasted, within type, size and count limits that are explained when refused.

Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line; the keys live in the send button's tooltip rather than on screen. While the model works, the button becomes Stop and Enter queues the message when onQueue is given.

name: Message response
purpose: Render a model's markdown reply while it streams.
notes: Streamdown keeps unfinished syntax readable mid-stream; every element uses kit typography, and fenced code uses the Code block.
Pass renderLink to route internal links with your router. Announce a finished reply once rather than letting a live region read each token.

name: Reasoning
purpose: Show a model's reasoning while it streams, then fold it away.
notes: Opens while the reasoning streams and closes when it ends, labelled with how long it took. Once the person opens or closes it, their choice stands.
It never takes focus, so reading the conversation is not interrupted. Pass the reasoning part's text and whether it is streaming.

name: Tool call
purpose: Show a tool call's state, parameters and result.
notes: The header names the tool and shows the AI SDK part state as a labelled badge: Preparing, Running, Needs approval, Done, Failed or Denied.
Closed by default, since the reply usually says what the call found; open it for failures. Pass a rendering of the result as children, or it shows JSON.

name: Sources
purpose: List the sources a reply drew on, folded behind a count.
notes: Numbered to match inline citations, with a short description of each. Links go through the host's link renderer, so internal ones route in-app.
It is the complete, keyboard-reachable record of a reply's sources; citation previews only repeat it.

name: Inline citation
purpose: Mark a claim with the sources behind it, in running text.
notes: A numbered link to the first source; hovering or focusing it previews every source it stands for. Consecutive numbers read as a range (2–4).
The preview holds no controls, because a hover card is not reachable by keyboard; the Sources list carries the same links.

name: Chain of thought
purpose: Report the steps an agent works through, as it goes.
notes: Each step shows done, in progress or not done, with results as chips. The whole list is open while a step runs and folds away when all are done.
Use it for progress an agent reports; use Tool call for the technical detail of one call.

name: Plan
purpose: Show what the assistant proposes to do, before it does it.
notes: A titled card with numbered steps and a detail per step, such as who it is for. The title shimmers while the plan streams.
It holds no actions: the decision belongs to a Confirmation directly below it.

name: Confirmation
purpose: Ask the person to approve a tool call before it runs, then record the decision.
notes: Pass the AI SDK tool part's state and approval.approved. Pending, it says what will happen and offers the two actions, the declining one first; afterwards it shows the outcome in place.
The approving action names what it does (Add tasks), not OK. Nothing changes until the person chooses.

name: Queue
purpose: Hold messages written while the assistant cannot take them.
notes: Sits above the composer. Each queued message can be removed; the label says when they will be sent.
Pair it with PromptInput's onQueue, so Enter queues during a reply instead of doing nothing.

name: Question
purpose: Let the assistant ask the person to choose before it continues.
notes: One option from a radio group, or the person's own answer when otherLabel is given. Submitting without an answer explains what is missing and focuses it.
Once answered, the form is replaced by the question and the answer. It never takes focus when it appears.

name: Attachments
purpose: Show files and records attached to a message.
notes: Images show as thumbnails; other files and references as chips with a name and a detail (size, or what the record is). With onRemove, each gets a remove button named after it.
The same chips appear in the composer and above the sent message, so what was sent stays visible.

name: Model selector
purpose: Choose the model for the next message.
notes: A quiet button names the current model; its list describes each model and marks the selected one. A search field appears once there are more than six.
Keep descriptions about behaviour the person will notice, such as speed or visible reasoning.

name: Context
purpose: Show how much of the model's context window a conversation uses.
notes: A ring in the composer opens a breakdown: tokens used of the window, the last input and output, and an estimated cost. It turns red past 80%.
It opens as a popover on click or keyboard, not a hover card, because it is a control rather than a link.

name: Message branch
purpose: Move between versions of a reply.
notes: Previous and next with the position between them (2 / 3); the count is announced as it changes. At either end the button stays focusable but inert.
Show it on the latest reply only, since earlier turns have already been answered from the version shown.

name: Checkpoint
purpose: Return a conversation to an earlier point.
notes: A quiet divider between turns whose Restore action appears on hover or keyboard focus, and always on touch screens.
Restoring removes what came after; pair it with Undo, and say what restoring does not reverse (changes the assistant already made).

name: Artifact
purpose: Hold something the assistant made for use outside the conversation.
notes: A titled surface: its actions sit in the header (copy, download, a labelled primary action), the content scrolls within a bounded height, and a footer records where it was used.
The title shimmers while the content streams; actions appear once it is complete.

name: Agent
purpose: Summarise an agent's configuration: model, instructions, tools and output.
notes: It describes; the controls that change the agent belong beside it. Tools show whether they are on and whether they ask first.
Keep instructions in the person's language: what the agent does and will not do.

name: Open in chat
purpose: Take a question about the current page to a chat.
notes: Your own assistant opens in-app with the question filled in; outside chats open in a new tab through chatLinks, and say so.
The question travels in the URL, so keep personal details out of it. Label each outside chat with its real mark.

name: Terminal
purpose: Show command output with its colours, following it while it runs.
notes: ANSI colour codes map to theme roles (error, success, warning, syntax), so output follows light and dark mode. Copy takes the plain text.
While streaming, the newest line stays in view unless the person scrolls up to read; a cursor marks that it is still running.

name: File tree
purpose: Browse folders and files, with changed files marked.
notes: The tree keyboard pattern: arrows move, open and close; Home and End jump; Enter or Space selects a file or toggles a folder. Only one row is in the tab order.
Added, modified and deleted files carry a letter that is also spoken.

name: Commit
purpose: Summarise a commit: message, hash, author and the lines each file changed.
notes: Additions and deletions are coloured and also stated in words for screen readers.
Pass the date already formatted; the component does not format or localise it.

name: Test results
purpose: Report a test run: the summary, a proportion bar and each test's outcome.
notes: Each test states its status in words as well as with an icon and colour.
details renders more under a test, such as a failure's Stack trace.

name: Stack trace
purpose: Show an error and where it happened, your code first.
notes: Frames marked internal (libraries, the runtime) fold behind a count, so the first useful line is never buried.
Paths wrap rather than truncate, keeping the line and column readable on narrow screens.
